title: Chapter 27. Nagari Padas — I: Vasu Ghosha (padas from the *Padakalpataru*)
html:
Introductory Note to the Section of Nagari Padas

"Nagari" (nāgarī) means a townswoman, a woman of Nadia; "nagara" (nāgara) is a townsman, a gallant, and in the language of Vaishnava poetry the beloved, the hero of the play of love (Krishna is so called: "Shyama-nagara," "rasika-nagara"). Nagari-bhava is the name given to the mood of padas in which the women of Nadia, having seen the young Gaura in the street, at the bathing ghat on the Ganga, in kirtana, tell their friends of His beauty, lose their peace, forget home, modesty and family, pine through the nights, see Him in dreams, and after His sannyasa lament the separation. In these songs Gaura is "Gauranga-nagara," "the nagara of Nadia." The imagery is taken from the padas on Radha and Krishna — purvaraga, anuraga, longing in expectation, disappointed waiting, telling a friend of the meeting; that is why in the Padakalpataru (PK) such padas stand as gaura-chandrikas (preludes) to the corresponding sections on Radha — marked "the words of the nagaris" (nāgarī ukti) — or are gathered into a separate pallava, "Gauranga's form: the words of the nagaris and others."

Who sang in this mood. Tradition regards Narahari Sarakara of Shrikhanda and Vasu Ghosha as the first singers of nagari-bhava (Majumdar remarks that Vasu calls Gaura "nagara" following Narahari); poets of the Shrikhanda school wrote in the same spirit, among them Narahari's disciple Lochana Dasa; later such padas multiply — Nayanananda, Yadunandana, and many songs signed "Narahari" in the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT), mostly by Narahari Chakravarti (18th century). Majumdar counts about twenty padas of Vasu Ghosha in PK as nagari-bhava; padas known only from GPT he considers unreliable (among them are even reworkings of padas on Krishna, ascribed to Vasu to give nagari-bhava an air of antiquity).

The position of the tradition. The Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura in the spirit of the nagaris. - Vrindavana Dasa in the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Adi-khanda), telling of the young Nimai, says that the Lord, who joked and played pranks with everyone, in this incarnation did not look at any woman even from the corner of His eye and would not even hear the word "woman"; therefore the wise, though every praise befits Him, do not glorify Him as "Gauranga-nagara," but sing of Him according to His nature. - Krishnadasa Kaviraja in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Adi 1.5–6; Adi 4) reveals the secret of this incarnation: Gaura is Krishna Himself, who has taken the bhava and the luster of Radha in order to taste the greatness of Her love, the sweetness of Himself that She tastes, and Her happiness. He came to taste Radha's love — as Radha, in the mood of a devotee — and not to enjoy the love of women as a hero. - Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati counts "gaura-nagari" among the apasampradayas — currents that have departed from the teaching of Mahaprabhu: worshipping Gaura as a nagara-lover transfers to His lila in Navadvipa what belongs to Krishna's Vraja-lila and distorts its meaning.

Gaura's attractiveness for all who saw Him is a quality of Bhagavan (so Krishna too is Madana-mohana, "the enchanter of the god of love himself"); the biographers also write that the Lord's beauty robbed the people of Nadia of their peace. But the Lord Himself in Navadvipa was a brahmana teacher, strict in conduct, then a devotee in Radha's bhava and a sannyasi; His lilas are not worldly love.

Rules of the section. (1) The nagari padas are translated for the completeness of the corpus of padas on Gaura and as a historical document — a witness to how He was sung of in the 16th–18th centuries; they are no basis for worshipping Gaura as a nagara. (2) The translation is faithful to the author: the text is neither softened nor heightened; where the original speaks of a glance and of beauty, it is so translated; where it speaks openly of attraction, it is translated exactly, with a note. (3) The heading of each pada is marked "nagari-bhava"; the notes give a brief reference to this note instead of the full caveat. (4) Pronouns referring to Gaura are capitalized; the nagaris' words about themselves are in lower case.

Chapter 27 contains the padas of Vasu Ghosha known from PK (the earliest and most reliable layer of nagari padas; Majumdar includes them in his list of Vasu's padas), in the order of the lila: Gaura's form through the eyes of the townswomen, first love and longing, a night of vain waiting, dreams and tales told to friends, the lament after the sannyasa. The text follows PK, checked against the scans, with the manuscript variants from PK's apparatus and the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.

1. Vasu Ghosha — "sajanī ai dekha śacīra nandana…" (PK 2151)

Nagari-bhava. Gaura's form: "Friend, look — there is Shachi's son!" Birds, beasts and trees weep hearing of His virtues, noble wives cannot hold their hearts steady; giving to all the name unattainable even for Brahma, Gora has delivered the world. In PK it stands in the pallava "Gaura's form." According to Majumdar, a pada of nagari-bhava. Raga varadi.1

সজনী ঐ দেখ শচীর নন্দন ।
যেবা জন দেখে তার স্থির নহে মন ॥ ধ্রু ॥

sajanī ai dekha śacīra nandana |
yebā jana dekhe tāra sthira nahe mana || dhru ||

sajanī — friend; ai dekha — look, there; śacīra nandana — Shachi's son; yebā jana dekhe — whoever sees; tāra — his; sthira nahe mana — the mind (heart) is not at peace

1.1(Refrain) Friend, look — there is Shachi's son:
whoever sees Him has no peace in his heart.

অসীম গুণের নিধি অপার মহিমা ।
এ তিন ভুবনে নাহি রূপে দিতে সীমা ॥

asīma guṇera nidhi apāra mahimā |
e tina bhubane nāhi rūpe dite sīmā ||

asīma guṇera nidhi — treasury of boundless virtues; apāra mahimā — endless glory; e tina bhubane — in these three worlds; nāhi — there is none; rūpe dite sīmā — to set a limit to the beauty

1.2A treasury of boundless virtues, His glory without end;
in the three worlds there is none who could set a limit to His beauty.

খগ মৃগ তরু লতা গুণ শুনি কান্দে ।
রূপে গুণে কুলবতী বুক নাহি বান্ধে ॥

khaga mṛga taru latā guṇa śuni kānde |
rūpe guṇe kulabatī buka nāhi bāndhe ||

khaga mṛga taru latā — birds, beasts, trees, creepers; guṇa śuni kānde — weep hearing of the virtues; rūpe guṇe — by the beauty and virtues; kulabatī — noble wives; buka nāhi bāndhe — cannot bind the breast (hold the heart steady)

1.3Birds, beasts, trees and creepers weep hearing of His virtues;
by His beauty and virtues noble wives cannot hold their hearts steady.2

ব্রহ্মার দুর্লভ নাম জনে জনে দিয়া ।
বাসুদেব বলে গোরা লইল তরিয়া ॥

brahmāra durlabha nāma jane jane diyā |
bāsudeba bale gorā laila tariyā ||

brahmāra durlabha nāma — the name unattainable for Brahma; jane jane diyā — giving to each person; bāsudeba bale — says Vasudeva; gorā — Gora; laila tariyā — has carried across (delivered)

1.4The name unattainable even for Brahma He has given to everyone —
says Vasudeva — so Gora has carried [all across the ocean of births].3

śrīgauracandrasya rūpa-barṇanaṃ" (description of Gaura's form), no. 43 (mark "॥৪৩॥২১৫১॥"); raga varadi; MS P-R-Sa no. 2258. GPT1 — p. 117, no. 20 (raga varadi); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 20 (catalogue: VG-183). Majumdar counts PK 2149–2155 among Vasu's nagari padas. Here the nagari motif is only "noble wives" (1.3); the rest is praise of Gaura, the giver of the name. On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section. hearts steady" (buka nāhi bāndhe, lit. "cannot bind the breast") — lose their peace. A common formula for describing beauty, as in the padas on Krishna; cf. chapter 23, note 7. Him as the yuga-avatara (cf. chapter 9, no. 1). MS "gha" in 1.2: "i" for "e" ("these [three worlds]"), "rūpera" for "rūpe" (same sense).

2. Vasu Ghosha — "sakhi he oi dekha gorā-kalebare…" (PK 2152)

Nagari-bhava. Gora's form from head to foot: a face more beautiful than many moons, arms like an elephant's trunk, a glance quicker than a wagtail, a sandal tilaka, garlands to the knees, a neck like a conch, a broad chest with necklaces, reddish feet, jewel-like nails; "the Creator fashioned this form to be the ruin of young women." Raga kamoda.4

সখি হে ওই দেখ গোরা-কলেবরে ।
কত চাঁদ জিনি মুখ সুন্দর অধরে ॥

sakhi he oi dekha gorā-kalebare |
kata cām̐da jini mukha sundara adhare ||

sakhi he — O friend; oi dekha — look, there; gorā-kalebare — Gora's form (body); kata cām̐da jini — surpassing many moons; mukha — the face; sundara adhare — with lovely lips

2.1Friend, look — there is Gora's form:
His face more beautiful than many moons, His lips lovely.

করিবর-কর জিনি বাহু সুবলনি ।
খঞ্জন জিনিয়া গোরার নয়ন-চাহনি ॥

karibara-kara jini bāhu subalani |
khañjana jiniyā gorāra nayana-cāhani ||

karibara-kara jini — surpassing the trunk of the best elephant; bāhu subalani — rounded arms; khañjana jiniyā — surpassing the wagtail; gorāra nayana-cāhani — the glance of Gora's eyes

2.2His rounded arms surpass the trunk of the best of elephants;
the glance of Gora's eyes surpasses the wagtail.5

চন্দন-তিলক সাজে সুচারু কপালে ।
আজানুলম্বিত চারু নব নব মালে ॥

candana-tilaka sāje sucāru kapāle |
ājānulambita cāru naba naba māle ||

candana-tilaka — a tilaka of sandal; sāje — adorns; sucāru kapāle — on the lovely forehead; ājānulambita — hanging to the knees; cāru naba naba māle — wondrous, ever-fresh garlands

2.3On His lovely forehead is a tilaka of sandal,
wondrous garlands, ever fresh, hang down to His knees.

কম্বু-কণ্ঠ পীন পরিসর হিয়া মাঝে ।
চন্দনে শোভিত কত রত্ন-হার সাজে ॥

kambu-kaṇṭha pīna parisara hiyā mājhe |
candane śobhita kata ratna-hāra sāje ||

kambu-kaṇṭha — a neck like a conch; pīna parisara hiyā mājhe — on the mighty, broad chest; candane śobhita — shining with sandal; kata ratna-hāra sāje — many jewelled necklaces adorn

2.4His neck is like a conch; on His broad and mighty chest,
anointed with sandal, are many jewelled necklaces.

রামরম্ভা জিনি উরু অরুণ চরণ ।
নখমণি জিনি ইন্দু পূর্ণ দরপণ ॥

rāmarambhā jini uru aruṇa caraṇa |
nakhamaṇi jini indu pūrṇa darapaṇa ||

rāmarambhā jini uru — thighs surpassing plantain stems; aruṇa caraṇa — reddish feet; nakha-maṇi — jewel-like nails; jini indu pūrṇa darapaṇa — surpass the full moon and a mirror

2.5His thighs are lovelier than plantain stems, His feet are reddish;
His jewel-like nails outshine the full moon and a mirror.

বাসুঘোষ বলে গোরা কোথা না আছিল ।
যুবতি বধিতে রূপ বিধি সিরজিল ॥

bāsughoṣa bale gorā kothā nā āchila |
yubati badhite rūpa bidhi sirajila ||

bāsughoṣa bale — says Vasu Ghosha; gorā kothā nā āchila — where was Gora not (where has Gora come from?); yubati badhite — to slay young women; rūpa bidhi sirajila — the Creator fashioned the form

2.6Says Vasu Ghosha: where has Gora come from?
The Creator fashioned this form to be the ruin of young women.6

MS P-R-Sa no. 2259. GPT1 — p. 117, no. 21 (raga kamoda); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 21 (catalogue: VG-009). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section. is a formula of the poetics of beauty (as in the padas on Krishna, "the enchanter of the god of love himself"), not a description of the Lord's deeds; cf. chapter 23, note 7. MSS "ka," "kha": "shines" (śobhe) for "adorns" (sāje, 2.3; so also GPT1); "kha": "body" (aṅga, 2.4).

3. Vasu Ghosha — "dekha dekha sakhi gorā bara dvijamaṇiyā…" (PK 2153)

Nagari-bhava. "Look, friend — Gora, the jewel of brahmanas!" With great patience the Creator made this peerless form: arms to the knees, a hue brighter than gold — is it ketaki, a golden lotus, champaka or a gem? His speech pours nectar; millions of moons offer themselves for His face; who, having seen Him, could walk away? Raga kanada.7

দেখ দেখ সখি গোরা বর দ্বিজমণিয়া ।
নিরুপম রূপ বিধি নিরমিল
কেমনে ধৈরজ ধরিয়া ॥ ধ্রু ॥

dekha dekha sakhi gorā bara dvijamaṇiyā |
nirupama rūpa bidhi niramila
kemane dhairaja dhariyā || dhru ||

dekha dekha sakhi — look, look, friend; gorā bara dvijamaṇiyā — Gora, the finest jewel of the twice-born; nirupama rūpa — the peerless form; bidhi niramila — the Creator made; kemane dhairaja dhariyā — with what patience (lit. "how, holding patience")

3.1(Refrain) Look, look, friend — Gora, the finest jewel of the twice-born!
With what patience
the Creator made this peerless form!8

আজানুলম্বিত সুবাহু-যুগল
বরণ কাঞ্চন জিনিয়া ।
কিয়ে সে কেতকী কনক-অম্বুজ
কিয়ে বা চম্পক মণিয়া ॥

ājānulambita subāhu-yugala
baraṇa kāñcana jiniyā |
kiye se ketakī kanaka-ambuja
kiye bā campaka maṇiyā ||

ājānulambita — reaching to the knees; subāhu-yugala — the two lovely arms; baraṇa kāñcana jiniyā — a hue surpassing gold; kiye se ketakī — is it ketaki; kanaka-ambuja — a golden lotus; kiye vā campaka maṇiyā — or champaka, a gem

3.2His two lovely arms reach to the knees,
the hue [of His body] outshines gold.
Is it ketaki, a golden lotus,
or champaka, or a gem?

কিয়ে গোরোচনা কুঙ্কুম-বরণ
জিনি অঙ্গ ঝলমলিয়া ।
মধুর বচনে অমিয়া বরিখে
ত্রিজগত-মন ভুলিয়া ॥

kiye gorocanā kuṅkuma-baraṇa
jini aṅga jhalamaliyā |
madhura bacane amiyā barikhe
trijagata-mana bhuliyā ||

kiye gorocanā — is it gorochana; kuṅkuma-baraṇa — of kunkuma hue; jini — surpassing; aṅga jhalamaliyā — the body shines; madhura bacane — with sweet words; amiyā barikhe — pours nectar; tri-jagata-mana bhuliyā — enchanting the mind of the three worlds

3.3Is its hue that of gorochana or kunkuma? —
no, the radiant body surpasses them.
With sweet words He pours down nectar,
and the mind of the three worlds is enchanted.9

কত কোটি চাঁদ বদন নিছনি
নখ-চাঁদে পড়ে গলিয়া ।
বাসুঘোষে কহে গৌরাঙ্গ-বদন
কে দেখি আসিবে চলিয়া ॥

kata koṭi cām̐da badana nichani
nakha-cām̐de paṛe galiyā |
bāsughoṣe kahe gaurāṅga-badana
ke dekhi āsibe caliyā ||

kata koṭi cām̐da — many millions of moons; badana nichani — offer themselves (nichani) for the face; nakha-cām̐de paṛe galiyā — melt, falling at the moons of the nails; bāsughoṣe kahe — says Vasu Ghosha; gaurāṅga-badana — Gauranga's face; ke dekhi āsibe caliyā — who, having seen, will walk away

3.4Millions of moons offer themselves for His face
and melt, falling at the moons of His nails.10
Says Vasu Ghosha: who, having seen Gauranga's face,
could walk away?

MS P-R-Sa no. 2260 (the word "finest," bara, is absent from it). GPT1 — p. 122, no. 32 (raga kalyani); GPT2 — sec. 3.1, no. 32 (catalogue: VG-127; row VG-126 has the same PK number). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section. "how can one keep one's composure?"; following the structure of the sentence ("the Creator made… how, summoning patience") we translate it as wonder at the Creator's painstaking work. comparisons for Gaura's golden body. and then given away (glossary): the moons are but a ransom for His face; "the moons of His nails" are His toenails, shining like moons.

4. Vasu Ghosha — "o nā ke bala go sajani…" (PK 2154)

Nagari-bhava. "Tell me, friend, who is this?" — a face lovelier than moons, a hue of gold and gem; the moon and the red lotus hide in shame before His nails, palms and feet; at the beauty of His brows Madana throws away his bow; a sidelong glance mixed with a smile strikes everyone; "beware — He has lit up the whole world." Raga (illegible in PK; in GPT1 varadi).11

ও না কে বল গো সজনি ।
কত চাঁদ জিনি সুন্দর মুখানি
বরণ কাঞ্চন মণি ॥ ধ্রু ॥

o nā ke bala go sajani |
kata cām̐da jini sundara mukhāni
baraṇa kāñcana maṇi || dhru ||

o nā ke — who is that; bala go sajani — tell me, friend; kata cām̐da jini — surpassing many moons; sundara mukhāni — the lovely face; baraṇa kāñcana maṇi — the hue is gold and gem

4.1(Refrain) Tell me, friend, who is this?
His lovely face is lovelier than many moons,
His hue is like gold and gem.

করি-কর জিনি বাহুর বলনি
আজানুলম্বিত সাজে ।
নখ কর পদ বিধু কোকনদ
হেরি লুকাইল লাজে ॥

kari-kara jini bāhura balani
ājānulambita sāje |
nakha kara pada bidhu kokanada
heri lukāila lāje ||

kari-kara jini — surpassing an elephant's trunk; bāhura balani — the roundness of the arms; ājānulambita sāje — reaching to the knees, it is lovely; nakha kara pada — nails, palms, feet; bidhu kokanada — the moon and the red lotus; heri — seeing; lukāila lāje — hid in shame

4.2The roundness of His arms surpasses an elephant's trunk,
reaching to His knees — how lovely they are!
The moon and the red lotus, seeing His nails, palms and feet,
have hidden themselves in shame.12

ভাঙ-যুগ বর দেখিতে সুন্দর
মদনে তেজয়ে ধনু ।
তেরছ চাহিয়া হাসি মিশাইয়া
হানয়ে সভার তনু ॥

bhāṅa-yuga bara dekhite sundara
madane tejaye dhanu |
teracha cāhiyā hāsi miśāiyā
hānaye sabhāra tanu ||

bhāṅa-yuga bara — the two fine arches of the brows; dekhite sundara — lovely to see; madane tejaye dhanu — Madana gives up his bow; terachha cāhiyā — glancing sidelong; hāsi miśāiyā — mixing in a smile; hānaye sabhāra tanu — strikes everyone (everyone's body)

4.3The two arches of His brows are so lovely
that Madana throws away his bow;
He casts a sidelong glance, mixing it with a smile —
and strikes everyone.13

কটিতে বসন অরুণ-বরণ
গলে দোলে বন-মালা ।
বাসুঘোষ ভণে হও সাবধানে
জগত কর্যাছে আলা ॥

kaṭite basana aruṇa-baraṇa
gale dole bana-mālā |
bāsughoṣa bhaṇe hao sābadhāne
jagata karyāche ālā ||

kaṭite basana — at the waist a cloth; aruṇa-baraṇa — of the colour of dawn; gale dole bana-mālā — on the neck sways a garland of forest flowers; bāsughoṣa bhaṇe — says Vasu Ghosha; hao sābadhāne — beware; jagata karyāche ālā — He has lit up the world

4.4At His waist is a cloth the colour of dawn,
on His neck sways a garland of forest flowers.
Says Vasu Ghosha: beware —
He has lit up the whole world!

(catalogue: VG-010). On nagari-bhava see the introductory note to the section.

the best elephant" (karibara-kara); "kha": "roundness" in the form subalani.

5. Vasu Ghosha — "dekhaha nāgara nadiyāra…" (PK 2155)

Nagari-bhava. "Behold the nagara of Nadia!" — His gait is sweeter than the step of a royal elephant; bee-like devotees fly to the fragrance of His lotus feet, and the whole world, drunk with honey, loses the directions; full of rasa, He smiles slightly, and at the arrow from the corner of His eye millions of Kamadevas swoon; the world is full of cries of "Glory to Gora!" Raga kamoda.14

দেখহ নাগর নদিয়ার ।
গজবর-গতি জিতি গমন সুমাধুরি
অপরূপ গোরা দ্বিজরায় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

dekhaha nāgara nadiyāra |
gajabara-gati jiti gamana sumādhuri
aparūpa gorā dvijarāya || dhru ||

dekhaha — behold; nāgara nadiyāra — the nagara of Nadia; gajabara-gati jiti — surpassing the gait of the best of elephants; gamana sumādhuri — a sweet gait; aparūpa gorā — wondrous Gora; dvija-rāya — king of the twice-born
